```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: Baverel P, Roskos L, Tatipalli M, Lee N, Stockman P, Taboada M,
  Vicini P, Horgan K, Narwal R. Exposure-Response Analysis of Overall
  Survival for Tremelimumab in Unresectable Malignant Mesothelioma: The
  Confounding Effect of Disease Status. *Clin Transl Sci.*
  2019;12(5):450-458.
  doi:[10.1111/cts.12633](https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.12633)
* Description: Two-compartment linear population PK model for
  tremelimumab (anti-CTLA-4 IgG2) in the DETERMINE trial of second- and
  third-line unresectable malignant mesothelioma.
* Modality: Therapeutic monoclonal antibody, IV infusion, 10 mg/kg every
  4 weeks for seven doses and every 12 weeks thereafter.

Baverel 2019 fitted a population PK model to the tremelimumab arm of the
phase IIb DETERMINE trial (NCT01843374) to derive each patient's
steady-state exposure, `AUCss = Dose / CL`, and then examined overall
survival (OS) by `AUCss` quartile. The apparent exposure-response trend
(median OS 4.9 months in the lowest quartile vs 14.9 months in the
highest) was attributed to confounding: sex, C-reactive protein (CRP) and
baseline tumor size were each associated with both OS and tremelimumab
clearance.

The OS analysis is Kaplan-Meier only (no parametric survival or hazard
model was fitted), so the packaged model is the PK model. The covariate
screen of Table 2 found sex, CRP and tumor size statistically significant
on clearance, but none changed `AUCss` by the pre-specified 30%, so the
authors' final model carries no covariates (Supplementary Figure S1
caption). The screened effects are recorded in the model's
`covariatesDataExcluded` metadata and reproduced below as a check.

```{r load-model}
mod <- readModelDb("Baverel_2019_tremelimumab")
mod_ui <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)
```

# Population

The PK data set had 376 tremelimumab-treated patients with 1,328
evaluable concentrations; six of the 382 randomized to tremelimumab had
no evaluable PK. Patients had unresectable pleural or peritoneal
malignant mesothelioma that had progressed after one or two prior
systemic regimens including a platinum agent. Baverel 2019 does not
tabulate age, weight, sex or race (those are in the primary trial report,
Maio et al., Lancet Oncol 2017); the Table 2 footnote gives the medians
used for covariate centring: serum albumin 31 g/L, CRP 33 mg/L and
baseline tumor size 97 mm. Fifteen of 377 ADA-evaluable tremelimumab
patients (4%) were ADA-positive after baseline, with no apparent effect
on PK.

```{r population}
str(mod_ui$meta$population)
```

# Typical-value profile under the DETERMINE regimen

The trial regimen was 10 mg/kg every 4 weeks for seven doses, then every
12 weeks. The infusion duration is not stated in Baverel 2019; a 1-hour
infusion is assumed (it has no visible effect on a 28-day profile).

```{r regimen}
dose_days <- c(seq(0, 6 * 28, by = 28), 6 * 28 + c(12, 24) * 7)
inf_dur <- 1 / 24

make_events <- function(ids, wt, dose_times, obs_times) {
  dose_rows <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = dose_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      amt = 10 * wt[id],
      rate = amt / inf_dur,
      evid = 1L,
      cmt = "central"
    )
  obs_rows <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

obs_profile <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 364, by = 1), dose_days + inf_dur)))
ev_typ <- make_events(1L, wt = c(70), dose_days, obs_profile)

sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_ui), events = ev_typ) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r typical-plot, fig.cap = "Typical-value tremelimumab concentration for a 70-kg patient under the DETERMINE regimen (10 mg/kg q4w x 7, then q12w)."}
ggplot(sim_typ, aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "Tremelimumab concentration (ug/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Virtual cohort

Body weight drives the dose (10 mg/kg) but not the PK parameters. Baverel
2019 does not report the weight distribution of the DETERMINE PK
population, so a log-normal weight with median 70 kg and 20% CV,
truncated to 40-130 kg, is assumed. One cohort of 200 patients is
simulated.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20190312)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20190312)
n_sub <- 200L
wt <- exp(rnorm(n_sub, log(70), 0.2))
wt <- pmin(pmax(wt, 40), 130)
summary(wt)
```

# Stochastic profile

```{r vpc}
obs_vpc <- seq(0, 364, by = 2)
ev_vpc <- make_events(seq_len(n_sub), wt, dose_days, obs_vpc)
sim_vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_ui, events = ev_vpc) |>
  as.data.frame()

vpc_sum <- sim_vpc |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    p50 = median(Cc),
    p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r vpc-plot, fig.cap = "Simulated median and 90% prediction interval of tremelimumab concentration (individual predictions, without residual error) under the DETERMINE regimen; 200 virtual patients."}
ggplot(vpc_sum, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "Tremelimumab concentration (ug/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Steady-state exposure (AUCss) and PKNCA

Baverel 2019 derived each patient's steady-state exposure as
`AUCss = Dose / CL` with the individual clearance (Supplementary Figure S1
caption), i.e. the AUC over one dosing interval at steady state for a
10 mg/kg dose. To check the packaged model against that metric with
PKNCA, the cohort is dosed 10 mg/kg every 4 weeks to steady state (ten
doses) and the AUC over the last 28-day interval (days 252-280) is
computed per patient.

```{r ss-sim}
tau_start <- 9 * 28
ss_doses <- seq(0, tau_start, by = 28)
obs_ss <- sort(unique(c(
  tau_start + c(0, inf_dur, 0.25, 0.5),
  seq(tau_start + 1, tau_start + 28, by = 1)
)))
ev_ss <- make_events(seq_len(n_sub), wt, ss_doses, obs_ss)
sim_ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_ui, events = ev_ss) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "10 mg/kg q4w")

ss_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod_ui),
  events = make_events(1L, wt = c(70), ss_doses, obs_ss)
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "typical 70 kg")
```

```{r pknca}
nca_input <- dplyr::bind_rows(sim_ss, ss_typ |> dplyr::mutate(id = 0L)) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, Cc)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_input, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  ev_ss |> dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = "10 mg/kg q4w"),
  data.frame(id = 0L, time = ss_doses, amt = 700, treatment = "typical 70 kg")
) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, amt)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = tau_start,
  end = tau_start + 28,
  auclast = TRUE,
  cmax = TRUE,
  cmin = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca_res)
```

The typical 70-kg patient checks the PKNCA AUC over one steady-state
interval against the closed form `Dose / CL` that Baverel 2019 used. Both
sides use the same parameters, so the agreement is limited only by the
trapezoidal integration and by any remaining accumulation.

```{r typical-auc-check}
auc_typ <- nca_tbl |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment == "typical 70 kg", PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::pull(PPORRES)
auc_closed <- 700 / 0.310
c(pknca = auc_typ, closed_form = auc_closed, pct_diff = 100 * (auc_typ / auc_closed - 1))
stopifnot(abs(auc_typ / auc_closed - 1) < 0.02)
```

# Comparison with Table 3 (AUCss by quartile)

Table 3 of Baverel 2019 gives the median `AUCss` within each quartile of
the 376 patients' model-predicted exposure. Q2 ends at 2,328 and Q3
starts at 2,331 mg/L.day, so the overall median is about 2,330 mg/L.day.
The simulated per-patient `AUCss` (PKNCA `auclast` over the steady-state
interval) is split into quartiles the same way.

```{r quartiles}
auc_sim <- nca_tbl |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment == "10 mg/kg q4w", PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::mutate(quartile = paste0("Q", dplyr::ntile(PPORRES, 4)))

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~quartile, ~auclast,
  "Q1", 1629,
  "Q2", 2118,
  "Q3", 2548,
  "Q4", 3404
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = auc_sim |> dplyr::select(quartile, PPTESTCD, PPORRES),
  reference = published,
  by = "quartile",
  units = c(auclast = "mg*day/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Median AUCss within each exposure quartile: Baverel 2019 Table 3 vs simulation. * differs from the reference by >20%."
)

overall_median <- median(auc_sim$PPORRES)
c(simulated_median = overall_median, published_median = 2330)
stopifnot(
  # A mis-transcribed CL or a unit error moves the whole distribution by
  # tens of percent. The assumed 70-kg median weight puts the expected
  # median at 700 / 0.310 = 2258 (-3%), and the median of 200 draws with
  # a log-scale SD near 0.43 has a sampling SE of about 4%, so 15% leaves
  # roughly three SEs of headroom across rxode2 builds.
  abs(overall_median / 2330 - 1) < 0.15
)
```

The simulated overall median (`r round(overall_median)` mg/L.day) is
`r round(100 * (overall_median / 2330 - 1))`% from the published value,
which is within the combined effect of the assumed 70-kg median weight
(-3%) and the sampling error of a 200-patient cohort. The simulated quartile
medians spread wider than the published ones (lower Q1, higher Q4).
That is expected: Table 3 summarises empirical Bayes estimates of
clearance from 1,328 sparse samples, which shrink toward the population
value, whereas the simulation draws clearance from the full 38% BSV.
The published Q4 also includes a few outliers (maximum 19,751 mg/L.day,
Supplementary Figure S2) that a log-normal draw of 200 patients does not
reproduce.

# Screened covariate effects (Supplementary Figure S1)

Table 2 reports the covariate effects that were tested on clearance as
proportional linear shifts from the cohort median
(`CL * (1 + coef * (COV - median))`) and, for sex, a fractional reduction
for women. Supplementary Figure S1 shows their effect on `AUCss` at the
10th and 90th percentiles. Recomputing the figure from the Table 2
coefficients confirms the reading of the coefficients recorded in
`covariatesDataExcluded`; the effects are not in the packaged model.

```{r figS1}
figS1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~covariate, ~level, ~cl_ratio, ~published_pct,
  "Female", "female vs male", 1 - 0.19, 24,
  "CRP", "121 mg/L", 1 + 0.0034 * (121 - 33), -22,
  "CRP", "4 mg/L", 1 + 0.0034 * (4 - 33), 10,
  "Tumor size", "201 mm", 1 + 0.00058 * (201 - 95.6), -6,
  "Tumor size", "36 mm", 1 + 0.00058 * (36 - 95.6), 4
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(recomputed_pct = round(100 * (1 / cl_ratio - 1), 1))

figS1 |>
  dplyr::select(covariate, level, recomputed_pct, published_pct) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Covariate" = covariate,
    "Level" = level,
    "AUCss change, recomputed (%)" = recomputed_pct,
    "AUCss change, Figure S1 (%)" = published_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Replicates Supplementary Figure S1 of Baverel 2019 from the Table 2 coefficients.")

stopifnot(all(abs(figS1$recomputed_pct - figS1$published_pct) < 1.5))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Final model is covariate-free.** Supplementary Figure S1 and the
  Results state that no covariate was kept in the final PK model, and the
  `AUCss` used for the exposure-response analysis came from that model.
  The Table 2 row labelled "Final model" (tumor size added to sex and
  CRP) is the last step of the covariate search, not the model used.
  The maintainers extracted the model the authors used for exposure
  derivation.
* **Table 1 BSV on CL (38.0%) equals the post-covariate value.** The
  Table 2 footnote says sex, CRP and tumor size reduced the CL
  variability "from 42% to 38%", yet Table 1 (titled the final model, with
  no covariate rows) prints 38.0%. Table 1 is extracted as printed; the
  covariate-free variability may be nearer 42%. The structural
  estimates of the covariate model are not reported separately.
* **BSV scale.** Table 1's column header "BSV (Omega) (%)" with the
  footnote "variance Omega^2" is read as `100 * Omega`, so each variance
  is `(BSV / 100)^2`. The alternative reading `log(1 + CV^2)` gives
  variances 6-7% smaller and does not change any conclusion here.
* **Residual error.** Proportional only (Supplementary Methods S1); the
  37.7% CV is the residual SD on the proportional scale.
* **Infusion duration** is not stated; 1 hour is assumed.
* **Body-weight distribution** of the DETERMINE PK population is not
  reported in Baverel 2019; a log-normal distribution with median 70 kg
  and 20% CV (40-130 kg) is assumed for the 10 mg/kg dosing.
* **Overall survival.** The OS analysis is Kaplan-Meier by exposure
  quartile and by baseline factor (Figures 1-3) with no fitted survival
  model, so there is no OS sub-model to package.
* **Screened covariates with no register column.** EORTC prognostic
  status (effect 0.068 on CL, P = 0.16) and epithelioid histology (8.4%
  higher CL, P = 0.19) are noted in the `population` metadata only.
* No erratum to Baverel 2019 was found in Europe PMC (checked
  2026-11-25).
